question.text: One of the stated purposes of NPO registration on SSE is to bring interested NPOs onto a 'common platform of legal requirements'. As SIA, Mr. Arjun Desai is explaining this to Nari Shakti Trust. Which of the following BEST captures the rationale?

answer.text: To force all NPOs to re-register under the Companies Act 2013 as Section 8 Companies
To harmonise disparate registration regimes (Trusts Act, Societies Act, Section 8) into a unified SSE qualifying framework for SSE access
To replace state-level charity commissioners with a central SEBI office
To mandate that all NPOs obtain ISO 9001 certification

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.1.2.1 recognises that NPOs possess a variety of legal structures and are regulated by various statutory bodies. The three-fold purpose FIRST point is to bring them onto a 'common platform of legal requirements for the purposes of accessing the SSE'. This is a HARMONISATION objective — NPOs retain their native legal form, but must meet a common set of criteria to access the SSE. The Trap: Option A wrongly forces re-registration. Option C wrongly proposes state-body replacement. Option D introduces ISO — irrelevant to SSE framework. Cross-Exam Context: This is a uniquely XXIII concept — not tested elsewhere. The harmonisation-without-re-registration design is distinctive of SSE. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When onboarding a trust registered under a niche state public-trust statute (e.g., Bombay Public Trusts Act 1950), verify that the state-law registration is treated on par with the central Trusts Act 1882 by the SSE. Table 3.1 row (b) explicitly covers state-law trusts, but some SSE officials have mis-interpreted this — keep the regulation extract handy.
